ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=37^\circ$, the perpendicular bisector of side $BC$ intersects $AC$ and $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively, and $AB=CD$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BD as shown in the diagram: \\
$\because$ DE is the perpendicular bisector of BC, and AB=CD, \\
$\therefore$ BD=CD=AB, \\
$\because$ $\angle$C=37$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DBC=$\angle$C=37$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ADB=2$\angle$C=74$^\circ$, \\
$\because$ AB=BD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$A=$\angle$ADB=\boxed{74^\circ},

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC with A near the upper left, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Segment BC is horizontal, D lies on side AC, and E lies on BC. Segment DE is drawn from D to E and has a right-angle mark at E, indicating DE is perpendicular to BC. The segment BD is not part of the original drawing, so draw BD as an auxiliary segment. Reasoning: Since DE is the perpendicular bisector of BC, every point on DE is equidistant from B and C; in particular, D lies on DE, so DB = DC. The problem gives AB = CD, hence AB = BD = CD. Since D lies on AC, angle BCD is the same as the given angle C, so angle BCD = 37°. In isosceles triangle BCD with DB = DC, the base angles at B and C are equal, so angle DBC = 37°. Because A, D, and C are collinear, angle ADB is the exterior angle of triangle BCD at D, so angle ADB = angle DBC + angle BCD = 37° + 37° = 74°. In triangle ABD, AB = BD, so the base angles opposite those equal sides are equal: angle BAD = angle ADB = 74°. Since AD lies along AC, angle BAD is angle A. Therefore angle A = 74°.
